Subject: Pilot Qs - retention caps / partial erasure for EU PHI

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing the compliance scoping for our EU pilot and have a few concrete questions that the legal and ops teams asked me to put in writing:

1) Retention caps: for PHI fields (patient name, MRN, free-text notes) — can Redwood enforce field-level retention windows per tenant, and what are typical minimum/maximum windows you support?

2) Partial erasure vs pseudonymization: for use-cases where we need to hide identities but keep records for analytics, do you offer a managed pseudonymization pipeline (deterministic tokenization + salt management) or would we need to run that ourselves before sending to the API?

3) Auditability: our auditors will require an immutable log proving when data was redacted/erased and which operator triggered it. Can Redwood export a tamper-evident audit trail (time-stamped, user id, action)?

4) Soft-delete timelines: if we request deletion, is there a configurable soft-delete/hold window (for legal hold) before physical purge? What are SLA expectations for irreversible purge?

We have a pilot start target of early March; for now we just need answers so we can draft the Data Processing Agreement addendum. If helpful I can share our proposed retention matrix.

Appreciate any detail you can share.

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and attaching our high-level playbook. Happy to discuss on a call next week.

1) Field-level retention: yes. Redwood supports tenant-scoped retention policies applied at field and route level. Typical windows we see in regulated clients: 30, 90, 180 days; we also support multi-year windows where required. Minimum configurable window is 1 day; maximum is customer-defined (no enforced hard upper limit from platform side), though longer windows can implicate audit/contractual requirements.

2) Pseudonymization: we offer two options:
  - Managed pseudonymization: Redwood can perform deterministic tokenization at ingest (we manage salts in customer-scoped KMS or optionally your own KMS). Tokens are reversible only with KMS-controlled keys and access policies; useful if you need reversible re-identification under strict controls.
  - Pre-ingest pseudonymization: customer performs tokenization before sending to API (recommended when you want zero re-id capability on our side).

3) Audit trail: the platform emits event records for redaction/erase actions with timestamp, API key/user id, route, and object id. We can export logs in newline-delimited JSON or provide a read-only export to your S3/GCS. For tamper-evidence we support signed audit bundles (timestamped and signed by Redwood's private key) that your auditors can verify.

4) Soft-delete and purge: we support configurable soft-delete TTL followed by physical purge. Typical pattern: soft-delete (immediate flag) + 30-day grace period (adjustable) before irreversible purge. Irreversible purge depends on where backups/replicas live (we document purge windows per environment and can include a clause in the DPA). For EU pilot we can commit to a documented purge timeline for dedicated/private deployments; shorter timelines for hosted tiers need contractual exceptions.

I've attached the playbook and a short matrix outlining trade-offs. Next steps: 1) confirm whether you prefer reversible tokenization (managed KMS) or customer-side tokenization; 2) confirm desired default retention windows per field class; 3) let me know preferred time for a 30m follow-up call.

Laura / team — quick technical confirmation and recommended defaults for the MediSys EU pilot.

Summary recommendations (can include in the DPA addendum):
- Managed pseudonymization flow:
  • We support deterministic tokenization at ingest. Salts/keys can be customer-managed (recommended) or Redwood-managed.
  • Keys are tenant-scoped; rotation is supported with re-tokenization window options (we can rotate keys without immediate re-id loss by maintaining a short overlap period).
  • Re-identification requires both the token store and the active KMS key; access is logged and gated by RBAC.

- Audit and tamper-evidence:
  • Audit events emitted to the customer's dedicated audit stream (S3/GCS) as newline-delimited JSON.
  • We produce signed audit bundles once-per-day for production tenants: a manifest + concatenated events signed with an HSM-protected RSA key (we can provide verification public key).
  • We retain detailed audit events for 7 years by default for enterprise contracts (configurable).

- Soft-delete + irreversible purge (recommended default for EU pilot):
  • Soft-delete: immediate flagging of objects (no read access from the normal API) + 30-day configurable hold.
  • Hold-extension / legal-hold: API to extend holds per object or tenant; legal holds bypass purge but remain recorded in audit.
  • Physical purge: after hold TTL, metadata + object shards are queued for secure wipe. For hosted tiers, purge is completed within 72 hours of queueing; for dedicated/private we can commit to 24 hours. We will include backup/replica purge windows in the DPA (typical replicated retention windows: up to 30 days beyond object purge unless contractually shortened).

- Backup/replica considerations:
  • Purge guarantees depend on where backups are stored. We recommend explicit DPA language for backup purge timelines.

- Operational controls for MediSys pilot:
  • We will enable tenant-scoped KMS (customer-provided) and daily signed audit bundles.
  • Default retention windows we suggest: Identifiers (name, MRN) = 90 days; Clinical notes (free text) = 180 days (customer can tighten).
  • Offer reversible re-id only for a named small list of admins and require two-person approval for re-id actions (logged).

I'll draft a short appendix for the DPA describing the above flows and the audit bundle format (manifest + signature + verification key). Attaching a short summary PDF for legal review.
